title: The Ninth Jedi Director Describes Creative Friction With Lucasfilm
excerpt:
Kenji Kamiyama says new rules emerged as his Star Wars anime expanded into a series.
Despite creative disagreements, he values the collaboration and hopes to continue the story.
body_md:
Director Kenji Kamiyama has discussed the challenges of expanding Star Wars: Visions Presents – The Ninth Jedi from a short-form concept into a full series. Speaking at the Aichi-Nagoya International Animation Film Festival, he recalled being promised substantial freedom early on, only to encounter additional Lucasfilm rules once the project grew into a longer production.

Kamiyama described moments of frustration and an angry response from Lucasfilm over the creative boundaries. Nevertheless, he expressed satisfaction with the overall experience. Working in the Star Wars universe had been a personal ambition, and he valued the chance to test his storytelling ideas with people whose work he admired.

The Ninth Jedi grew out of the Star Wars: Visions anthology and became an eight-episode limited series on Disney+. Its alternative approach to the franchise's distant timeline and mythology makes the balance between artistic freedom and established franchise rules particularly important.

The filmmaker has expressed interest in a second season, noting that the writing process revealed more story potential than could fit into the initial run. That interest should not be mistaken for a renewal announcement: the report does not confirm that Disney or Lucasfilm has ordered another season.
